ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the pulley is located at point O, and the light rope passes around the pulley; the rope segment on the right side connects horizontally from the pulley to the wall at A, and the other segment connects vertically downward from the pulley to the heavy object C. The light wooden rod BO is oblique upward to the left from near the pulley axle, and the angle between BO and the vertical direction is marked as θ in the figure. Then reason: isolate only the pulley to analyze the forces. The tension in the light rope is equal everywhere; let it be T. Since the heavy object at end C is in equilibrium, T is equal to the magnitude of the weight of the heavy object. The rope has two pulling forces on the pulley: one along the direction of the horizontal rope segment, and the other along the direction of the vertical rope segment; the magnitudes of the two are both T, and the angle between them is 90°. Therefore the magnitude of the resultant force of the rope on the pulley is √(T²+T²)=√2T. The mass of the pulley can be ignored and it is in equilibrium, so the magnitude of the force exerted by the wooden rod on the pulley must be equal to the magnitude of the resultant force of the rope on the pulley, namely √2T. When θ is changed, the position of the pulley is unchanged, the directions of the horizontal rope segment and the vertical rope segment are unchanged, and the weight of the heavy object is unchanged, so T is unchanged, and the angle between the two tensions is also unchanged. Therefore the magnitude of the force exerted by the wooden rod on the pulley does not change with θ.

method.method_draft: 先读图：滑轮位于 O，绳子一段从滑轮水平连到右侧墙上 A，另一段从滑轮竖直向下连到重物 C；木杆 BO 斜向上方，θ 是 BO 与竖直方向的夹角。再读题：滑轮质量可忽略，轻绳绕过滑轮，系统平衡；改变的是木杆 BO 的方向角 θ，但保持滑轮位置不变。解题时只隔离滑轮受力：绳的张力处处相等，设为 T，且由重物 C 平衡知 T 等于重物重力大小。绳对滑轮有两个大小均为 T 的拉力，一个沿水平绳段方向，一个沿竖直绳段方向，两者夹角由图中绳段方向决定为 90°，不随 BO 的角度改变。因此绳对滑轮的合力大小为 sqrt(T^2+T^2)=sqrt(2)T。滑轮本身平衡，所以木杆对滑轮的作用力大小必须等于这个合力大小，即 sqrt(2)T。由于 T 和两段绳的夹角都没有因 θ 改变而改变，所以木杆对滑轮的作用力大小不变。
